_about: The story score: how every Sunday option is scored blind and ordered, as rows (the story engine v5 plan, 26 Nov 2026; docs/proposals/2026-11-26-story-engine-gaps.md). Three stages in a fixed order: the floor (scripts/post-pack/story_floor.py, config/story-floor.json: the only reader of his rejections, pass or refused, never a number), the blind score (scripts/post-pack/story_score.py: anchored 0-10 axes, weighted per content type out of 100, with hard floors per type) and the council on close calls only. Taste is a floor only (Ruling, Krish, 2026-11-26): nothing here reads his picks, his approved taste, why_here, cues, scorecards or his verdicts on formats, and nothing is tuned from his picks automatically. Weights and anchors are a first proposal from the growth evidence below and the rulings; only Krish changes them, by a pull request. A weight, anchor, floor, margin or cost is a row here, never code.
from_note: The first board the Sunday gate holds to the score (codes story and story_floor). 2026-11-30 if this merges before the 29 Nov run; earlier boards keep the order they were made in.

rulings.ruling: His taste is a floor only: his rejections refuse an option, never score it, and the judges stay blind (check-judges.ts section 4, tests/story_wall_test.py).
The blind proof run spends at most $10, through the ledger, after the protocol is committed.
The approved North Star reader line (config/beat.json reader), his words: "I approve the lines".

The off days are the reader's world too: a good-news carousel, a meme, a short and an off-day carousel each hold the fit floor as a hard floor (config/beat.json offdays), his words: "Make sure all the good news suggestions and meme suggestions are also aligned to the new positioning, as well as the carousels."

Every Monday, Wednesday and Friday carries one wildcard option he could pick: a real, dated, primary-sourced story on the beat, far from the obvious takes, its distance checked by the divergence engine, never asserted (the wildcard row below; idea_checks.wildcard_findings), his words: "Just make sure my Monday, Wednesday, and Friday stories: there's always one completely divergent, strange, obscure, or unexpected story suggestion that I could pick from."

blind_view._about: What the scorer and every blind judge may see of an option (story_score.blind_view): only the keep fields, and inside them never a drop_nested key. Where it came from, who asked for it, what anyone said of it and whether it was recommended are never seen; his-first on equal totals is the only place the order reads where an option came from.

strip_text._about: Provenance wording inside the kept fields: words that say an option came from him (what he saved, asked for or improved). Applied to every string the blind view keeps, the source label included (story_score.strip_text); story_proof.strip_house runs the same rules first, then its card-only ones. patterns are taken out where they stand, in order; then a sentence still matching drop_sentences_matching is dropped. A string no rule touches comes back as it was.

abstain.note: Of 10: an option whose read axes carry less weight than this is unscored (total null), never ranked on what little was read.

primary_sources._about: A primary source is on the actor's own site (a name in the option's topic or fact is the site's name) or on a filing or paper host below.

anchors.10: Changes money, rights or work for a whole sector or for millions of fans and creators, with a sourced figure.
anchors.7: A major named player's move with a measurable second-order effect on others in the sector.
anchors.4: One notable company or creator, with a local consequence.
anchors.1: Trivia, a personnel move or a version bump.

axes.label: Absurd or funny on its own true facts

anchors.10: The plain sourced fact is absurd on its face and the best sound angle reads as supported humour, no explaining needed.
anchors.7: The fact carries a clear incongruity or reversal a stranger gets at once.
anchors.4: A wry detail is there but needs a line of set-up.
anchors.1: Nothing funny in the facts; any joke would cost credibility.

anchors.10: Nobody else is telling it this way, it is specific to this story and the reader can use it today.
anchors.7: A fresh, specific take with one rival telling it nearby.
anchors.4: A familiar take with one specific detail added.
anchors.1: The take every outlet already ran.

anchors.7: Three documented rungs plus labelled inferred ones that reach five, landing open.

anchors.4: A focus-sector keyword only in the body.
anchors.1: No focus-sector keyword anywhere (the avoid list is the floor's, not a score).

anchors.7: Clearly helps a named group, at a modest scale.
anchors.4: Helps, but the people helped are vague.

anchors.10: Dated inside the edition week and first reported this week.
anchors.4: Last week, with a new development this week.

floor_rows: A floor is hard unless it says hard false: a hard floor that fails puts the option last and fails the Sunday gate (story_floor). A floor marked hard false is a note: reported beside the score (story_score.notes) and in the Sunday summary, never failing the gate or moving the order. The plan's hard floors are the series floors (a Monday's sourced money figure, a Wednesday's mechanism rung, a Friday's counter rung), the whys floors, a short's and a meme's humour, and the template and good-news checks; fit on the off-day types (good news, meme, short, explainer) is hard by ruling offday_beat (Krish, 2026-11-26); a hero's fit and a primary source were added as floors without a ruling, so they are notes until Krish rules them hard. The wildcard's four floors (truth, sources, beat, whys) are hard by ruling wildcard (Krish, 2026-11-26), so a strange but thin story cannot hide behind the label; it has no series floor. if_read: a floor whose value is not there (an explainer with no steps) is not read, never failed.

divergent.problem: Angles on one true story for {audience}. Each angle rests on a fact in the story as quoted below; never add a detail the story does not give. The story: {what}
divergent.score_problem: Angles on true stories for {audience}. Which is the most original, useful and specific way to tell each story, judged on the words alone?

angle.humour_margin_note: On the 0-10 angle score: the funniest or most absurd true angle (comic_reading supported, mechanism in absurd_mechanisms) wins over the best angle only when sound and within this margin.

close.margin_note: Of 100: a slot's top two within this are a close call.
close.fork_note: Also close: both within 8 and one leads on absurdity_humour by 3 or more while the other leads on scale or whys by 3 or more.

council.barred_note: The ai-harness council's When it runs section admits Krish's ask or the strategist only, so until a ruling adds this caller a close call shows as close call, your pick, never a silent pass (commit 0 readiness).

briefs._about: The words of the briefs the blind judges and the council read (story_score.py brief and council-brief). Internal, never published.
judge: You are a blind judge. You see one story at a time and nothing about who suggested it, who will pick it or what anyone said about it.
Score each axis named under a story from 0 to 10 against its anchors. Use the anchors as the scale: 10, 7, 4 and 1 are described; anything between is fine.
Reply with one line per axis, exactly: <axis>: <n>/10 because <the evidence in the story that earns it>.
Put the story's key on its own line before its scores, as: ## <key>.
Judge only what the story says. A number with no evidence after because is not counted. British spelling, no em dashes, no exclamation marks.
briefs.fun_produce: For fun_produce, these are the formats the channel can make (catalogue) and what held people on the channels (growth evidence). Judge whether a format fits and whether there is something to show, not say.
council: Two story options, A and B, for the same slot. They scored within a close margin. Only the facts on record are below: nothing about who suggested either, nor any earlier choice.
Run every seat: Offer, Attention, Experience, Scale, Distribution. For each seat write one line: <Seat>: A Score <n>/10 (fact|assumption); B Score <n>/10 (fact|assumption).
Then the chair's call on its own line: Chair: A, B or unknown, because <the reason>.
British spelling, no em dashes, no exclamation marks.

unit_costs._about: Dollars reserved in the week's ledger before each call (files.ledger). After a served divergent call the reservation is settled to the metered cost: the route's own cost figure when its answer gives one, else the chain's change over the call (divergent.chain_week) when that is more than the reservation, never less, since the chain may lag; with neither, the reservation stands and the call's metered field says so. A humour read keeps its reservation: the humour engine's answer names no cost. A settled cost over its reservation counts at once, so the next call is refused when it leaves no room. score_judge is the route's up-front estimate ($0.10) with headroom for up to 4 model calls at the model's price (commit 0 readiness, control-center api/_divergent.ts).

spend.note: Under the route's 20 quick ops and $5 a day, and the $15 weekly chain (config/chain-cap.json). The chain cap is checked first; over any cap the call is refused and the step is reported skipped, never passed.

growth_evidence._about: Performance data, not taste: what held people on the channels, read only from krishanraja/growth-makeyourmindup. Read by the fun_produce judge and the named_thing anchors.

wildcard._about: The day's wildcard (ruling wildcard, Krish, 2026-11-26). Every hero day the board shows carries at least min_per_day options with "wildcard": {"kind": one of kinds, "why_unexpected": one line of what makes it far from the obvious takes, "divergent": {"run_id", "spark"} when it came from the engine, "distance": what divergent.py distance recorded}. It is a real, dated, primary-sourced story on the beat and passes the fact gate, the floor, its own floors in types.wildcard and the refute pass like any option. The order may place it anywhere and never drops it; it need not beat the day's top score. Its distance is checked, never asserted: divergent.py distance scores it free (obvious given, no judge) against the day's other options and the worn ground; a status in divergent_statuses is divergent, the engine's own spark in the archive (own_spark) is expected, anything else refuses the board (code wildcard, from the from date); not served is recorded as skipped and the session's why_unexpected stands, said in the run summary. The board shows it by board_prefix at the start of its pitch question (it passes idea_checks.question_problems).

distance.problem: The {day} story for a publication on {about}, for the week of {week}: an idea far from the obvious takes on it

files._about: Where the story score keeps its working files, inside docs/plans/<Monday>-week/. The spend ledger is under the gitignored .cache/, one file per week ({week} is its Monday), so budget_usd and --budget-usd cap a week's run, not every week ever run; usd_per_day and divergent_ops_per_day are read from the same file. An explicit --ledger (the blind proof's .cache/proof/story-engine-v5/spend.jsonl) is read whole: the proof's $10 is for the whole proof.
